description.narrative: The objective of the COVID-19 (Coronavirus) Emergency Response Project is to prevent, detect and respond to the threat posed by COVID-19 (Coronavirus) and strengthen national systems for public health preparedness in Ethiopia. There are five components to the project, the first component being medical supplies and equipment. This component will finance the procurement of medical supplies and equipment needed for activities outlined in the EPRP such as (i) case management; (ii) infection prevention and control; and (iii) other pillars of the strategic plan. The second component is the preparedness, capacity building and training. This component will finance activities related to preparedness, capacity building and training, guided by the different pillars and activities of the EPRP. The third component is the community discussions and information outreach. Activities supported by this component include: risk communication and community engagement; behavioral and sociocultural risk factors assessments; production of RCCE strategy and training documents; production of communication materials; establish a production center for information and communication tools production center (media and community engagement); and monitoring and evidence generation; and human resources for risk communication. The fourth component is the quarantine, isolation and treatment centers establishment. Activities supported by this component include: establishing isolation and treatment centers, including provision of nutrition and dignity kits to quarantined patients, and equipping them with medical supplies and furniture and network installation. Finally, the fifth component is the project implementation and monitoring.
To prevent, detect and respond to the threat posed by COVID-19 and strengthen national systems for public health preparedness in Ethiopia.

Schedule 2, Section I, B, 2(a): By no later than one (1) month after the Effective Date, prepare a draft work plan and budget forProject implementation, setting forth, inter alia: (i) a detailed description of the planned activities, including any proposedconferences and Training, under the Project for the period covered by the plan; (ii) the sources and proposed use of fundstherefor; (iii) procurement and environmental and social safeguards arrangements therefor, as applicable and; (iv) responsibilityfor the execution of said Project activities, budgets, start and completion dates, outputs and monitoring indicators to trackprogress of each activity

title.narrative: Number of health workers deployed for COVID-19 preparedness and response.

comment.narrative: The factors for the large deployment of health workers during the COVID-19 pandemic include: the intensity and unpredictable nature of the pandemic itself necessitated a massive mobilization of personnel. Furthermore, in many regions, the pandemic coincided with existing or new humanitarian crises, further stretching resources and demanding additional health worker deployments. The rapid implementation of emergency workforce adaptations, such as the redeployment of staff and the recruitment of volunteers and retired professionals, significantly increased the overall number of health workers involved in the response.

comment.narrative:
To enhance the safety monitoring of vaccines, comprehensive guidelines and Standard Operating Procedures have been developed and communicated to relevant stakeholders. The following guidelines have been developed for consistent and effective pharmacovigilance practices: * National Guideline for Monitoring Adverse Events Following Immunization (AEFI) * Vaccine Safety Risk and Crisis Communication Guideline * Guideline for Consumer Reporting of Adverse Events of Medicines and Vaccines
Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) developed and implemented: * SOP for Adverse Drug Event Reports and AEFI Receiving and Processing * SOP for Investigation of AEFIs * SOP for Causality Assessment of Adverse Event Reports
